failing_scenario: An informative image element is missing the alt attribute entirely.
recommendation: Add a descriptive alt attribute to all informative elements. The alt text must convey the meaning or purpose of the image — not describe its visual appearance. Guideline: Be concise, specific, and avoid starting with 'Image of' or 'Picture of'.

failing_scenario: An informative image has alt="" (empty alt text), hiding meaningful content from screen reader users.
recommendation: Replace the empty alt attribute with meaningful alternative text that conveys the purpose and information of the image. Empty alt (alt="") signals a decorative image — using it on an informative image causes the content to be skipped entirely by screen readers.

failing_scenario: An decorative image element is missing alt="" (empty alt), causing it to be announced by screen readers.
recommendation: Add alt="" (empty alt text) to all decorative elements so assistive technologies skip them. Do not use alt=" " (a space) as some screen readers will still announce it. A decorative image is one that adds no information — e.g., visual dividers, background textures, or purely stylistic icons.

failing_scenario: A decorative <svg> icon is missing aria-hidden="true", causing it to be read aloud by screen readers.
recommendation: Add aria-hidden="true" and focusable="false" to all decorative <svg> elements. Also remove any <title> or <desc> elements from decorative SVGs, as these may still be announced. For functional SVGs (e.g., icon buttons), provide aria-label on the parent control instead.
code_after:
<button class="close-btn" aria-label="Close dialog">
  <svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">
    <use href="#icon-close"></use>
  </svg>
</button>

failing_scenario: An image-only button or link is missing an accessible name — no alt, aria-label, or aria-labelledby is provided.
recommendation: Provide an accessible name for every interactive image element using one of these methods: 1. Add a meaningful alt attribute to the inside the button/link. 2. Add aria-label directly on the

failing_scenario: A complex image (chart, graph, or infographic) has only a brief alt text and is missing a long text description.
recommendation:
For complex images, provide a short alt text AND a detailed long description that conveys the same information as the image. Use one of these approaches:
  1. aria-describedby referencing a visible or hidden description element.
  2. A visible <figcaption> within a <figure> element.
  3. A link to a separate page with the full data.

The long description must convey all data, trends, and key insights from the image.

failing_scenario: An element has non-descriptive alt text (e.g., 'image', 'photo', filename, or a URL) that does not convey the image's content.
recommendation:
Replace vague or non-descriptive alt text with meaningful alternative text.

Rules for good alt text:
  - Convey the information or function of the image
  - Do not start with 'Image of', 'Picture of', or 'Graphic of'
  - Do not use the filename or URL as alt text
  - Keep it concise (typically under 150 characters)
  - Match the context in which the image appears

failing_scenario: User-uploaded images (e.g., in a chat or post feature) do not provide an option to add alternative text at the point of upload.
recommendation:
Provide an alt text input field at the point of image upload. Include:
  1. A text field for the user to enter alt text.
  2. A checkbox to mark the image as decorative (skips alt text requirement).
  3. Store and render the user-provided alt text in the img element when displayed.

Prompt the user with clear guidance on what good alt text looks like.
code_before:
<!-- No alt text option provided -->
<input type="file" accept="image/*" id="upload">
code_after:
<label for="img-upload">Upload Image</label>
<input type="file" id="img-upload" accept="image/*">

<label for="img-alt">Alternative text</label>
<input type="text" id="img-alt"
       placeholder="Describe the image for screen reader users">

<label>
  <input type="checkbox" id="img-decorative">
  This image is decorative (no alt text needed)
</label>

failing_scenario: An decorative image contains alt text that is duplicative of adjacent visible text, causing redundant screen reader announcements.
recommendation:
When an image is purely decorative and adjacent text already conveys the same information, set alt="" (empty) on the image so screen readers do not repeat the content.

Example scenario: A checkmark icon next to the word 'Confirmed' — the icon adds no additional information and should have alt="".
code_before: Next Confirmed
code_after: Next Confirmed

failing_scenario: A CSS background-image conveys meaningful information without a visible text alternative or programmatic text description.
recommendation: CSS background images cannot carry alt text. If the image is meaningful, use one of: 1. Replace with an inline element and add a descriptive alt attribute. 2. Add a visually-hidden inside the element with the same information. 3. Use aria-label on the container element. If the background image is purely decorative, no action is needed.
